question: Does RackTrack show me CVEs or security advisories for my switch?
answer:
No. RackTrack shows no CVEs, severity badges or vulnerability counts anywhere — CVE reporting was removed from the product, and the server deliberately ignores the advisory rows the lookup agent still carries.

The closest thing: on the Firmware screen, after a check, tap "Show details" and read "Release notes excerpts". If the vendor's notes for the newer release mentioned security fixes, they appear as a "Security fixes in <version>" block, next to Bug fixes, New features, Known issues and Deprecations.

For a real vulnerability assessment use your vendor's advisory page or your own security tooling. RackTrack answers "is there newer firmware and what changed", not "am I vulnerable".
rootCause: server/app.js maps the agent's FirmwareAdvice onto the /api/firmware contract and explicitly skips advice.advisories; the only security-flavoured output is the target release's security_fixes list rendered as a changelog section.

question: Where is the "Firmware Check" screen? I can't find it in the menu.
answer:
There is no menu entry for it — /firmware is a URL-only route. The sidebar has Home, Scan, Two racks, Profile (plus Console/Lab for the platform owner and Data Sources/Marketplace for admins), and the phone bottom bar only has HOME, SCAN, PROFILE.

Use the switch card instead: open the rack, click Switches in the sidebar, pick your switch, and open its Firmware tab (next to Specifications and SFP Advisor). The version is filled in for you from the scan or the CMDB.

If you want the standalone page anyway, type /firmware onto the end of the app address. You will have to type Make / Vendor, Model and Current version by hand — it knows nothing about your rack. Either way you must be signed in.
rootCause: The /firmware route is registered in App.jsx and has a page title entry in DesktopShell, but no NavLink in the desktop sidebar links array or the mobile BottomNav items, so it is URL-only.

question: The Firmware tab says "No firmware version recorded" or "Add a model to check for updates" — why won't it check?
answer:
The check needs all three of vendor, model and version. It never calls the server until it has them (the endpoint itself rejects a missing one with "vendor, model, and currentVersion are required").

1. "Add a model to check for updates." — use "Enter make / model" (or "Add model" / "Add vendor") at the top of the card.
2. "No firmware version recorded." — tap "Enter version", type what the switch is running (e.g. 1.0.6 Build 20210323), Save. The check starts straight away: "Checking for updates…".
3. If you save a version and nothing happens, the vendor is what's missing, not the version. Fill the vendor in at the top of the card and it will run.

Use "Edit version" next to the Firmware heading to change it later. Anything you type here is stored in this browser only.
symptoms: Add a model to check for updates
rootCause: loadDetails() sets firmwareStatus='skipped' unless displayVendor and lookupModel resolve, and again unless a cleaned version exists; POST /api/firmware itself 400s with 'vendor, model, and currentVersion are required'.

question: The check worked but "Release notes excerpts" shows 0 and says it couldn't extract anything. Is that a bug?
answer:
No, that's expected. We got a version number for your device but no written-out release notes to break into sections, which is normal for most vendors — the long-tail lookup only returns a version pointer and never invents bullet points.

Under "Show details", the number next to "Release notes excerpts" is how many blocks we found. "Couldn't fetch release notes: …" means the vendor page couldn't be read at all; "Couldn't extract any changelog sections from the page." means we had nothing to split up. Either way, use "Search release notes ↗" or "Open page ↗" just below to read the vendor's page yourself.

When excerpts do exist they appear as Security fixes, Bug fixes, New features, Known issues and Deprecations, each labelled with the newer version.
symptoms: Couldn't extract any changelog sections from the page
rootCause: changelog[] is synthesized only from the target release's security_fixes/bug_fixes/new_features/known_issues/deprecations arrays; when those are empty (the usual case for the live 'pointer tier' lookup, which never synthesizes bullets) the section falls back to the empty state plus search links.

evidence.snippet: Release notes excerpts {result.changelog?.length || 0} ... {result.releaseNotesError ? `Couldn't fetch release notes: ${result.releaseNotesError}` : "Couldn't extract any changelog sections from the page."}

Search release notes ↗
...
                              Open page ↗

Returns a *version pointer* (version, optional release_date, notes_url).
Bullet-level diff (security/features/bugs) is **not** synthesized — that
requires either a hand-built per-vendor fetcher (Cumulus / MikroTik) or
an LLM, and we have neither for the long tail. Honest by design.

question: The Firmware Check screen says "Vendor list unavailable: …" under the Make / Vendor box.
answer:
Only the vendor type-ahead failed to load. The firmware check itself is unaffected — the vendor you type is sent as-is and never checked against that list.

1. Type the vendor as the manufacturer writes it (Cisco, Juniper, Aruba).
2. Fill in Model and Current version — all three fields are required — and tap "Check firmware".
3. To get the list back, reload the screen; it is fetched once on open.
4. If it fails for everyone it is server-side, not your phone. "Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment." means the vendor-sheet lookup on the server hit its 90-second limit. Report the exact text after "Vendor list unavailable:".

(Evidence line fix: server/app.js — the 90s timeout block is at 6964-6987 and GET /api/specs/vendors at 7011-7013, not 6887-6907 / 6934-6940.)
symptoms: Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment.
rootCause: FirmwarePage fetches /api/specs/vendors once on mount; that endpoint shells out to pipeline.all_vendor --list-vendors, which reads Switch_Vendors_Websites.xlsx and is killed after PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS (90s). Failure only disables the suggestion list.

question: The Switch Info pop-up has its own "Firmware Update" card — is that different from the Firmware tab on the switch card?
answer:
Same lookup, different source for the current version.

The "Firmware Update" card in the Switch Info pop-up (header: "Switch Info · live · <host> · <vendor>") reads the version live off the switch over SSH — it pulls "Firmware Version" / "Software Version" out of the device's system output, trims it ("5.0.2 Build 20220909 Rel.75392" → "5.0.2") and then runs the same vendor check as the switch card.

Only the wording differs: "Up to date", "Upgrade available", or "Could not determine latest version", with Current version / Latest version rows and a "Release notes" link. While it runs: "Checking vendor site for newer firmware…". If the SSH read gave no model or version: "Need both model and firmware version to check for updates." If the lookup failed: "Could not check: …".

The Firmware tab on the switch card uses whatever the scan/CMDB recorded or what you typed — it never talks to the switch. So if the two disagree, the pop-up is the one showing what's actually running.
symptoms: Checking vendor site for newer firmware
Need both model and firmware version to check for updates
rootCause: ResultsPage's SwitchInfoModal parses firmware from the live SSH system-info output, runs cleanFirmwareVersion() on it and calls the same POST /api/firmware; it renders its own headline set independent of SwitchInformationPage's fwHeadline.

question: How current is the firmware data, and how often does it refresh?
answer:
There is no automatic refresh — nothing in the server schedules a firmware update.

• "Latest version" comes from the agent's SQLite cache at Agent/Agent_scrap/data/switches.db, which is only filled when someone runs `python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py` by hand. No cron, timer or startup hook calls it.
• Dedicated public fetchers exist for exactly three vendors: MikroTik (RouterOS), Ubiquiti (UniFi OS), NVIDIA (Cumulus Linux). Every other vendor falls back to a best-effort live web lookup with an 8.5-second deadline, whose result is written back into the same cache.
• On the client, each firmware result is held in a module-level Map keyed by rack + vendor + model + version, with no expiry. Reload the tab to force a fresh call.

So a firmware answer is only as current as the last manual fetcher run (or, for non-fetcher vendors, the last live lookup that succeeded).
symptoms: how old is the firmware data
rootCause: Firmware/advisory ingestion is a manually-invoked script (Agent_scrap/scripts/fetch_firmware.py); server/app.js has no scheduler for it, and the client cache in scanPrefetch.js is a module-level Map with no TTL.

evidence.snippet:
python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py                 # all public vendors
    python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py mikrotik        # one vendor
    python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py mikrotik -v     # verbose
    python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py nvd             # CVE data from NIST NVD
    python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py kev             # CISA actively-exploited overlay

question: A switch shows "Upgrade available" but the Latest version we display is the same age or older than what the customer is running. Why?
answer:
The badge means "different from our cached value", not "you are behind" — there is no version comparison anywhere in the path.

The server computes it by literal string equality (server/app.js:7265-7267, in firmwarePayloadFromAgent):

    upToDate = String(agentLatest).trim() === String(req.currentVersion).trim();

Anything not byte-identical — 16.12.1 vs 16.12.01, a trailing build suffix, different case — is false, and the UI paints "Upgrade available" (client/src/pages/SwitchInformationPage.jsx:449-452).

It can also fire when our cached "latest" is older than the customer's version. When the per-NOS changelog diff is empty, the agent falls back to `_synthetic_diff_from_latest` (Agent/Agent_scrap/firmware.py:750-767), which returns the cached vendor-level latest unconditionally with releases_behind=0 rather than suppressing it. A stale or wrong cached pointer therefore surfaces as a false "Upgrade available".

Handling: read the two version strings back to the customer, explain the badge is a cache mismatch, and point them at the release-notes / vendor link. Do not tell them they are behind.
symptoms: says upgrade but we are newer
rootCause: firmwarePayloadFromAgent computes upToDate by exact trimmed string equality; the agent's _synthetic_diff_from_latest returns the cached vendor-level latest unconditionally with releases_behind=0.

question: Which vendors do we actually have firmware data for, and what does a customer see for the rest?
answer:
Three tiers, and it is about vendor *reachability*, not a supported-device list.

1. Real changelogs — only MikroTik (RouterOS), Ubiquiti (UniFi OS) and NVIDIA (Cumulus Linux). These are the only vendors with a working public fetcher.

2. Login-gated — Cisco, Juniper, Arista, HPE Aruba, Dell, Fortinet, plus the registry's gated list (Huawei, H3C, Lenovo, Tejas, ZTE, NEC, Fujitsu, ALE, RUCKUS, Extreme, Ciena, Nokia). Full release notes need a vendor login, but we still return NVD CVE data and a portal URL. The card shows "Recommended min: X" if we know a fix version, otherwise "Check vendor portal" with a "Vendor portal ↗" link.

3. Everything else — a best-effort live web lookup (8.5s deadline) that yields a latest-version pointer only, never a changelog. If it misses, the advisor returns "No firmware data available for <vendor>" (or "No NOS specified and no default known for <vendor>") and the card reads "Latest version unknown".

Source: Agent/Agent_scrap/firmware.py (PUBLIC_FIRMWARE_VENDORS 539, LOGIN_GATED_VENDORS 571, live fallback 703/846, messages 725-730 and 861-865); client/src/pages/SwitchInformationPage.jsx:448-461.

which vendors are supported for firmware
rootCause: firmware.advise() branches on PUBLIC_FIRMWARE_VENDORS / LOGIN_GATED_VENDORS and otherwise falls through to live_firmware_lookup, returning has_data=False with a vendor-specific message when all tiers miss.

question: How much can we trust the "Latest version" values the shipped agent database returns?
answer:
Very little — treat the shipped cache as demo-grade, not authoritative. Never quote it to a customer as a firmware recommendation.

The `firmware_versions` table in `Agent/Agent_scrap/data/switches.db` holds 16 rows, all written by the generic `firmware_fetchers` scrape, and several are plainly mis-scraped: HPE Aruba is stored as version "802.3af" (a PoE standard) with a picclick.com listing as its release-notes link; Cisco as "16.2" pointing at a Nexus 9336C-FX2 model page; MikroTik as "25.6196C16"; Netgear as "36.75ZM17". Every row also has `nos` set to the vendor name rather than a real network OS, and `release_date` is null on all but one.

Why: the fetcher regex-matches any version-like token on a search-result page and upserts it with no validation against the real vendor NOS (`live_firmware.py:29`).

Consequence: lookup is by vendor alone (`firmware.py:192 vendor_latest_any`), so any customer on one of those 16 vendors gets a bogus "Latest", a false "Upgrade available" (`server/app.js:7265` — plain string comparison), and a junk "Release notes" link. Fix is to re-run the fetchers or curate the rows; there is no in-app override.
symptoms: release notes link goes to picclick
rootCause: The generic live/pointer fetcher regex-matches any 'version-like' token on a search-result page and upserts it into firmware_versions with source='firmware_fetchers'; nothing validates the match against the real vendor NOS, and the shipped DB was populated from those runs.

question: "Couldn't check for updates right now" — what actually failed on the server?
answer:
POST /api/firmware shells out to the Python agent CLI (Agent/Agent_scrap/cli.py) and collapses every failure into {ok:false, error} served with HTTP 404 (server/app.js:7230-7237). The switch card shows one generic line for all of them (SwitchInformationPage.jsx:786); the Firmware Check page prints the raw string in its red banner (FirmwarePage.jsx:108). Read that string:

- "agent not installed at Agent/Agent_scrap" — cli.py missing; the agent is cloned separately, not part of this checkout (app.js:7326, 7339).
- "Agent lookup took too long." — exceeded AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000 and was SIGKILLed (app.js:7334, 7348).
- "Agent failed to start." — spawn error: wrong pythonCmd / missing interpreter (app.js:7355).
- "Agent returned no parsable JSON." — last stdout line wasn't JSON; last 500 chars of stderr attach as _stderr for the server log only (app.js:7363).
- "Agent failed to return a firmware response." — agent replied but with no usable advice object (app.js:7258).

Not agent failures: HTTP 400 "vendor, model, and currentVersion are required" is a missing-field pre-flight; "Backend returned a non-JSON response (HTTP …)" and "Request failed: … Is the backend running on port 3001?" are client-side network errors (FirmwarePage.jsx:104, 114).
symptoms: Couldn't check for updates right now
Is the backend running on port 3001
rootCause: runAgentCli() resolves a small set of fixed error strings; firmwarePayloadFromAgent passes them through as payload.error and the route replies 404 when ok is false. SwitchInformationPage collapses all of them to one generic status line; FirmwarePage prints the raw string.

evidence.snippet: {firmwareStatus === 'error'   && <StatusLine color={statusColor}>Couldn't check for updates right now.</StatusLine>}

question: Is pipeline/firmware_overrides.json still used for the "latest known firmware" values?
answer:
No — it is dead data. Nothing in the repo reads it.

Its own header (pipeline/firmware_overrides.json:2) claims it is "consulted before web scraping in pipeline.firmware_check" and is "the authoritative source for the 'latest known firmware' badge", but no pipeline/firmware_check.py exists and a repo-wide grep for `firmware_overrides` returns only the file itself.

The real path is server/app.js:7204 (POST /api/firmware) → runAgentCli(['--firmware', '<vendor> <model>', currentVersion]) at app.js:7229, which hits the Agent_scrap SQLite DB (app.js:7322).

So editing rows there — e.g. the Cisco C9300 "17.15.3" / lastChecked 2026-05-08 entry — changes nothing a customer sees. To fix a wrong "Latest" value, update the agent's DB; this file should be wired in or deleted.

where do the latest firmware numbers come from
rootCause: pipeline/firmware_overrides.json documents an integration with pipeline.firmware_check that does not exist in this repo; the live firmware path is server/app.js → runAgentCli('--firmware') → Agent/Agent_scrap.

question: Are the firmware and vendor lookup endpoints authenticated?
answer:
No. In server/app.js, GET /api/specs/vendors (7012), POST /api/specs (7023) and POST /api/firmware (7204) are all registered with no auth.requireAuth — unlike neighbouring routes such as GET /api/cmdb/rack/:rackId/switches (5114). The client sends a token via authFetch, but the server never checks it.

Each call also spawns a Python child process: /api/firmware goes through runAgentCli (AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000, line 7334), /api/specs/vendors through runPipelineModule (PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000, line 6964). The only rate limiter in the file, uploadLimiter (line 38), is applied to scan/detect/auth only (474, 481, 492) — never to these routes. So an unauthenticated caller can hold open long-lived Python processes and drive outbound web scraping from our host.

Internal only — do not mention to customers. Hardening item: add requireAuth plus a rate limit before any public exposure of the API host.
rootCause: The spec/firmware routes were added without the auth.requireAuth middleware used elsewhere in app.js, while each handler shells out to a Python child process with a 60-90 second wall-clock budget and no throttling.

app.get('/api/cmdb/rack/:rackId/switches', auth.requireAuth, (req, res) => {

const PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000;

function runPipelineModule(moduleName, extraArgs) {
